project_inclusion.note: Locally useful look-alike; strict native-status filtering deferred.

morphology_keys.life_cycle: Annual or short-lived perennial depending on treatment/conditions.
morphology_keys.habit: Twining vine with long flexible shoots.
morphology_keys.leaves: Alternate, large, heart-shaped; often 3-lobed; densely to moderately hairy.
morphology_keys.sepals: Usually about 16–17 mm in Williamson County material, lanceolate and hairy.
morphology_keys.corolla: Large trumpet-shaped flower, around 5–7 cm or more across/long in local material; often blue-violet aging pinkish.
morphology_keys.key: Much larger flower than I. hederacea and I. triloba; hairy foliage and long sepals.

field_diagnostics.single_best_trait: For I. nil versus I. hederacea, compare sepal architecture before leaf shape: nil sepals are long, densely hairy basally and narrow gradually toward a mostly straighter distal portion, with a usually larger flower.
fastest_traits: Sepals densely hispid near the base and gradually narrowed distally

look_alikes.distinction: Lengths overlap, so use shape: I. hederacea sepals are broader basally then abruptly narrow into conspicuously curved/spreading tips; I. nil sepals narrow more gradually and are generally straighter. Nil also tends toward the larger corolla.
I. lindheimeri is perennial with a very large 55–90 mm flower, long 18–30 mm sepals and strongly lobed hairy foliage; use habit and flower/sepal scale.
